entities.name: Operation Ten-Go
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
Operation Ten-Go was a pivotal 1945 Japanese naval operation in World War II, exposing the vulnerability of Japan's main naval force in the Pacific Ocean.

On April 7, 1945, the United States launched Operation Ten-Go's precursor, a massive aerial assault, which crippled Japan's naval capabilities. This strategic blow led to the decisive Battle of Okinawa, where Allied forces seized crucial island strongholds.

The consequences of Operation Ten-Go rippled forward, as the weakened Japanese fleet failed to counter the US naval superiority. This military imbalance ultimately contributed to Japan's unconditional surrender to the Allied Powers on September 2, 1945.

As the last remnants of the once-proud Japanese navy were destroyed, the seeds of a new era were sown, marking the beginning of post-war Japan's transformation into a global economic power.
